newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Trinidad's Panday back from India, sees trade rise.
newsitem.headline: Trinidad's Panday back from India, sees trade rise.

text.p: PORT OF SPAIN, Feb 6, Reuter - Prime Minister Basdeo Panday returned home tonight from a 12-day official visit to India, his ancestral home, and told reporters he was certain trade and investment would increase between Trinidad and Tobago and India as a result of his visit.
Panday said several companies from that country have expressed interest in setting up plants in this Caribbean state.
Indian businessmen plan to visit this country over the next three months to follow up discussions, he declared.
The prime minister was accompanied on the trip by two ministers and a group of local businessmen.

Commenting on the controversy surrounding his government's nomination of Ray Robinson to contest the Feb 14 presidential election, Panday said the former prime minister "has been a distinguished servant of Trinidad and Tobago and on that basis, he is a good choice for the presidency."
The Opposition People's National Movement (PNM) party has objected to the government's nominee, saying "an active politician should not considered for the job."
Robinson was prime minister from 1986 to 1991, and is currently Panday's deputy in the 15-month coalition government.
Panday said his government did not intend to withdraw Robinson's nomination.
The PNM has named as its candidate a high court judge, Anthony Lucky, to contest the election.
Trinidad and Tobago's current president, Noor Hassanali, aged 78, is due to retire on March 19 after holding office for ten years. He is a former high court judge.
